evidence_articles.title: Names of people belonging to Matua, minority communities deleted from post-SIR voter rolls: Mamata - The Hindu
evidence_articles.rephrased: **Mamata Banerjee**, West Bengal Chief Minister, accused the **Union government** of targeting specific communities by deleting names from voter rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) proce
evidence_articles.content: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday (April 7, 2026) alleged that names of people belonging to the Matua and minority communities were deleted from the post-SIR voter rolls in the State. Addressing a rally at Chakdaha in Nadia district, Ms. Banerjee said that the TMC will stand by those whose names were excluded from the voter rolls, following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Assembly elections April 7, 2026 LIVE: Campaigning ends in Kerala, Assam, Puducherry today According to the latest data by the Election Commission of India (ECI), nearly 91 lakh voters have been deleted from the electoral rolls in West Bengal after the SIR process. The poll panel is yet to announce the finally altered voter base for the state after the roll revision process. As per official data released on February 28, 63.66 lakh names, around 8.3% of the electorate, were deleted since the SIR process began in November last year, reducing the voter base from about 7.66 crore to just over 7.04 crore. Accusing the Centre of discrimination, Ms. Banerjee alleged that names were being removed from voter rolls by targeting specific communities. “Why this discrimination? You are excluding Matuas, Rajbanshis and minorities. Do you think that people do not understand this?” the CM said. She also claimed that in districts with significant minority population such as Murshidabad, Malda and North Dinajpur, names were “picked and removed like lice” from the electoral rolls. Ms. Banerjee asserted that following her intervention in the Supreme Court, around 32 lakh names out of nearly 60 lakh cases under ‘adjudication’ had been restored. “Those whose names are still missing should apply before the tribunal. The TMC will stand by you and provide legal support,” she said. Questioning the Centre’s stand on infiltration, Ms. Banerjee said the Union government has the responsibility of protecting the country’s borders, but it was blaming the West Bengal government for infiltration. Describing the upcoming Assembly polls as a battle to protect people’s identity and democratic rights, the TMC supremo urged voters to respond through the ballot. “This election is a fight to save your democracy, language and respect so that no one can ever call you a foreigner,” Ms. Banerjee said. At another poll rally in Bongaon, the CM asserted that the Trinamool Congress will win more seats than before, and form government for the fourth consecutive term. “The TMC will ultimately win and get more seats than before,” she said. The party had won 215 seats in the 2021 elections for the 294-member West Bengal assembly. “This election is to avenge the deletion of names from the voter list,” Ms. Banerjee said. The TMC chief claimed that names of 300 members of Missionaries of Charity, which was formed by Mother Teresa, have been deleted in the electoral rolls revision exercise, and also those of monks of the Ramakrishna Mission and Bharat Sevasram Sangha. Ms. Banerjee also said that several names have been excluded from the rolls in Murshidabad, Uttar Dinajpur, Malda, South 24 Parganas and Nadia districts, while reiterating that in Bhabanipur constituency, where she is contesting for re-election, 40,000 names have been struck off. “We will have to see how many names have been restored in the supplementary list... I will not allow detention camps to be set up (in Bengal). Constitutional rights must be given, and I will continue to fight for restoration of these,” she said. In a bid to woo the Matua community, who have a strong presence in several assembly constituencies in North 24 Parganas and Nadia district, Ms. Banerjee said that her government has initiated a lot of development works in those areas. The CM also accused the BJP of trying to divide Matua community votes. Attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Ms. Banerjee claimed that he had lunch with leaders of Gulf countries and hugged them, with religion not becoming a barrier. “When you go to Gulf countries, you hug the Muslim rulers,” she said. Ms. Banerjee also claimed that cattle are exported from the country, but it does not become an issue as to whether that is right or wrong. “Their (BJP) religion is to divide votes, that is not Hinduism,” the TMC chief added. Published - April 07, 2026 02:08 pm IST

recent_articles.title: Trinamool rebellion revives government hopes of passing Delimitation Bill - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** internal dissent, particularly within its parliamentary party, has reignited speculation about the government's potential introduction of the Delimitation Bill during the Monsoon Session in mid-July. The bill, aimed at redrawing electoral boundaries based on the 2011 census, failed to secure a two-thirds majority in Parliament in April and was accompanied by the Women’s Reservation Amendment Bill, which also fell short.

recent_articles.title: INDIA bloc to take SIR complaints to CJI; seeks Pradhan’s immediate exit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The INDIA bloc, led by **Congress** president Mallikarjun Kharge, met to discuss concerns over the special intensive revision (SIR) and alleged 'vote loot'. The meeting saw criticism of the Congress's handling of the recent Rajya Sabha election in Bihar, with leaders calling for a more concrete organizational structure.  The bloc also discussed the post-poll violence in West Bengal and called for an all-party meeting to address the current economic situation. **Mamata Banerjee**, who led the charge for unity after her party's defeat in the recent Assembly elections, urged the alliance to respond to youth protests under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party.  The bloc will meet again in August.

recent_articles.title: Unity in diversity: On the INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-three Opposition parties**, including the **Congress**, **Samajwadi Party**, and **Trinamool Congress**, met in New Delhi on Monday to address concerns about economic distress, inflation, and educational chaos.  The bloc resolved to write to the Chief Justice of India over electoral fraud allegations, demand the resignation of the Union Education Minister, call for an all-party meeting to discuss the economic crisis, agree to hold coordination meetings every two months, and commit to daily parliamentary coordination during sessions. The meeting followed recent fissures within the alliance, including the absence of the **DMK** and the **Aam Aadmi Party**, highlighting the fragility of the coalition.  Despite these challenges, there is a broad consensus on the need to checkmate the **BJP** for political survival and the health of Indian democracy.

recent_articles.title: Unity in diversity: On the INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twenty-three Opposition parties**, including **Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge** and **Leader of the Opposition (Lok Sabha) Rahul Gandhi**, met in Delhi on Monday to address concerns about economic distress, inflation, and educational chaos. The bloc resolved to write to the Chief Justice of India regarding electoral fraud, demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, call for an all-party meeting to address the economic crisis, agree to hold coordination meetings every two months, and commit to daily parliamentary coordination.  The meeting aimed to strengthen institutional framework for Opposition coordination and press the ruling **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** on governance failures.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Split, Cracks In INDIA Bloc: Hardeep Puri Says Next Target Punjab
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hardeep Singh Puri**, Union Minister, stated that the **INDIA alliance** is facing internal contradictions and appears to be unravelling. He cited public criticism of **Mamata Banerjee** by **Rahul Gandhi** and the resignation of Trinamool Congress MP Sukhendu Sekhar Roy as evidence of this weakening.  Puri believes the BJP's recent victory in West Bengal has emboldened them to contest half the seats in Punjab, where they are targeting the AAP government's fiscal irresponsibility, law and order issues, and drug crisis. He predicts that the alliance will continue to struggle, with more constituent parties drifting toward new formulations.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Split, Cracks In INDIA Bloc: Hardeep Puri Says Next Target Punjab
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Hardeep Singh Puri**, Union Minister, stated that the **INDIA alliance** is unraveling due to internal contradictions and party conflicts. He highlighted the Trinamool Congress's internal revolt, exemplified by the resignation of MP Sukhendu Sekhar Roy, citing corruption, political killings, and atrocities against women as reasons for his exit.  Puri also criticized the AAP government in Punjab for fiscal irresponsibility, worsening law and order, and a deepening drug crisis. He predicted that the **INDIA alliance** will "stutter along," with more constituent parties drifting toward new formulations.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Rebel, 10 MPs Meet BJP Leaders As Mamata Banerjee Attends INDIA Meet
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** is facing internal unrest following their defeat in the West Bengal assembly elections. At least 20 of its 41 MPs are reportedly in contact with the **BJP**, possibly planning to defect, and a closed-door meeting between at least 10 rebel MPs and **BJP** leaders in Delhi has intensified the turmoil. The rebels, including Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Shatabdi Roy, and others, plan to inform the Speaker tomorrow that they are the "real Trinamool" and form their own bloc within parliament.  This shift in focus from West Bengal to Delhi comes after reports of dissent within the party, with some MPs refusing to attend party activities or addressing their leader by her usual title.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Rebel, 10 MPs Meet BJP Leaders As Mamata Banerjee Attends INDIA Meet
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** MPs are reportedly planning to defect from the party after their recent election defeat in West Bengal, with at least 20 of the 41 MPs possibly joining forces with the **BJP**.  A closed-door meeting between these rebel MPs and **BJP** leaders is taking place in Delhi, led by **Shatabdi Roy**, **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar**, and others. The rebels aim to form a separate bloc within Parliament and are planning to inform the Speaker of their intentions tomorrow. This internal unrest follows reports of dissent among party members, including some MPs who have switched off their phones or attended meetings with opposing figures.

recent_articles.title: After Bengal Defeat, Is Mamata Banerjee Preparing For National Politics?
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, after a difficult election in West Bengal, is shifting her political focus to national opposition coordination through the **INDIA alliance**. This move comes after the 2026 assembly elections and following internal divisions within the Trinamool Congress.  She is actively attending **INDIA** meetings, seeking to build broader solidarity among opposition parties and position herself as a cooperative participant in the anti-BJP platform rather than a direct leader. The goal is to leverage national issues like unemployment, inflation, and foreign policy to counter the BJP's narrative. This strategy aims to address internal party concerns and regain lost political ground both within West Bengal and nationally.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Congress Crisis Sharmila Sarkar: "20 Trinamool MPs Forming New Bloc, Will Support NDA": Rebel MP To NDTV
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar** and 20 other **Trinamool Congress** MPs plan to join the **NDA coalition**, formally writing to Speaker **Om Birla**. The group, led by **Ghosh Dastidar** as chief whip, will form a separate bloc with **Shatabdi Roy** as deputy leader. This move follows similar actions in West Bengal where 58 MLAs formed a rival bloc, mirroring the Shiv Sena's strategy.  The decision comes after discussions and is seen as a response to Mamata Banerjee's leadership style and recent party decisions.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool rebellion reaches Delhi: 20 party MPs in talks with Union Minister Bhupendra Yadav - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several Trinamool Congress MPs, including Howrah MP Prasun Banerjee and Bankura MP Anup Chakraborty, held a meeting at **Bhupendra Yadav’s** residence on June 8th, 2026. The meeting, which included 20 Lok Sabha MPs, aims to form a separate bloc and support the BJP-led NDA government.  The rebellion comes after nearly 60 Trinamool MLAs elected Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of Opposition, signaling a growing rift within the party. **Suvendu Adhikari**, who was likely present at the meeting, is emerging as a potential leader of this new bloc.

recent_articles.title: INDIA Bloc Meet Live Updates: Pointed Fingers Or Alliance Unity? All Eyes On Delhi Meeting
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **23** opposition parties are expected to meet in Delhi on Monday to discuss their strategy for the upcoming state and national elections. The meeting, called "Janbandhan," will focus on uniting against the **BJP** and addressing differences between alliance partners.  The **Congress**, **AAP**, **DMK**, and **TVK** are among the parties expected to attend.  **Mamata Banerjee** of the **TMC** is likely to raise concerns about attacks on her party's leaders in Bengal, while **John Brittas** of the **CPI(M)** will address alleged political understanding between the Left and the **BJP** during the Kerala polls.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Rajya Sabha MP Sukhendu Sekhar Roy resigns, says ‘I was unhappy in party’ | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sukhendu Sekhar Roy**, a veteran Trinamool Congress leader, resigned from the party and his Rajya Sabha seat citing long-standing internal issues.  He stated he will make a decision about joining another party after introspection. **Mamata Banerjee** and her nephew, **Abhishek Banerjee**, are in Delhi for an INDIA opposition bloc meeting following the Trinamool's significant defeat in the West Bengal Assembly election.

recent_articles.title: Falta's 'Pushpa' Jahangir Khan Arrested By Bengal Special Task Force
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jahangir Khan**, a Trinamool strongman, was arrested at the India-Nepal border after being on the radar of law enforcement for alleged threats and election fraud attempts.  Khan had been previously granted interim protection by the Calcutta High Court but it was revoked following the filing of five police cases against him. He had withdrawn from the Falta constituency re-election after allegations of voting machine tampering, branding himself as "Pushpa" in reference to a Telugu action thriller character. **Abhishek Banerjee**, an MP and close aide of **Mamata Banerjee**, has been linked to Khan's activities.  Khan’s arrest follows his withdrawal from the election contest shortly before the re-election.

recent_articles.title: Mamata Banerjee meets Kejriwal ahead of INDIA bloc meeting - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, chief of the **Trinamool Congress**, met with **Arvind Kejriwal**, convener of the **Aam Aadmi Party**, in Delhi on Sunday. The meeting, described as "warm," focused on the future direction of the opposition bloc **INDIA**.  The two leaders discussed the road ahead for the group, which will meet on Monday to strategize against the BJP and address differences arising from recent Assembly election results.

recent_articles.title: DMK absent, allies restive, INDIA bloc braces for a difficult conversation at today’s meeting | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Opposition INDIA bloc is set to meet in Delhi on Monday, facing a weakened position after the recent Assembly elections and internal tensions. The absence of the DMK due to its disagreement with the Congress over the Tamil Nadu government's formation has added to the complexity.  **Mamata Banerjee**, **Abhishek Banerjee**, and other leaders are expected to play a mediating role as the bloc grapples with issues including electoral rolls, delimitation, simultaneous elections, education system concerns, and coordination.

recent_articles.title: 4,800 illegal infiltrators deported to Bangladesh, says Bengal CM Suvendu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced that **4,800** individuals deported from India to Bangladesh over the past month were not covered by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. He stated that these individuals were handed over to the **Border Security Force** under a law used in other states but not applied in West Bengal, where they were treated as guests and lodged in prisons.

recent_articles.title: Eggs thrown at Trinamool leaders, workers as public anger mounts in Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** (TMC) MLA Madan Mitra was targeted by public anger over accusations of corruption. On Saturday night, June 6, 2026, eggs were thrown at his convoy in Kamarhati constituency. The incident has sparked further public discontent and highlighted the ongoing tension between citizens and local party workers following the TMC's defeat in the 2026 West Bengal Assembly election.

recent_articles.title: After TMC MLAs, MPs may be next: Mamata lands in Delhi amid fears of a repeat in Parliament | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, the **TMC** chief, arrived in Delhi to meet with **Arvind Kejriwal** and discuss the future of the INDIA bloc.  She is facing a potential split within her party as some MPs are reportedly dissatisfied with **Abhishek Banerjee**, the parliamentary party leader. Sources indicate that a section of MPs may approach Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Monday, while others are in contact with him to explore options. The rebels have confidence that 20 MPs will join them, but **Mamata** believes at least 16 MPs will remain loyal to her.

recent_articles.title: Brahmananda Chakraborty Video: Trinamool Leader Hid Under Sarees To Evade Arrest. Then This Happened
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** leader Brahmananda Chakraborty was arrested in Howrah, West Bengal after residents accused him of illegally collecting commissions from a government housing scheme.  Residents filed a complaint alleging that Chakraborty had siphoned off funds from the scheme by taking unofficial commissions from beneficiaries.  Chakraborty attempted to evade arrest by hiding beneath a pile of sarees but was apprehended by police during a search operation.

recent_articles.title: INDIA Bloc To Meet Tomorrow - A Regrouping After Assembly Polls, DMK Walkout
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** announced that 23 parties will attend a strategy meeting to prepare for the upcoming monsoon session of parliament, which is expected to begin in July. **MK Stalin**, DMK leader, confirmed his party's absence due to alliance issues. The meeting comes amid speculation that the government might reintroduce two Constitution Amendment Bills previously failed to pass during the budget session.  The **CPM** will also attend, while **Mamata Banerjee**, **Akhileh Yadav**, and **Tejashvi Yadav** are expected to be present.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Councillor Arrested For Sexually Harassing Minor
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohammad Jasimuddin**, a Trinamool Congress councillor, was arrested in Kolkata on Sunday for molestation and harassment of a minor girl.  Police forced entry into his locked house after waiting six hours, arresting him under multiple sections of the POCSO Act and BNS. This arrest follows the filing of a complaint by the victim's family alleging harassment three years ago, and another complaint filed on Saturday. **Jasimuddin**, who previously served with the CPI(M), joined the Trinamool Congress in 2015 and won two consecutive elections.  The incident has sparked tension in the area with protests from his followers and supporters of the BJP.

recent_articles.title: INDIA Bloc Meet Tomorrow, Mamata Banerjee Eyes Help From Frenemy Congress
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leader Jairam Ramesh announced that 23 political parties will participate in the INDIA bloc's meeting tomorrow, with some parties declining attendance due to their own reasons. **DMK** and **AAP**, led by MK Stalin and Arvind Kejriwal respectively, are not attending due to political differences and recent alliance changes.  The meeting is being held at the Constitution Club in Delhi at the behest of **Trinamool Congress** leader Mamata Banerjee who needs support from the bloc to fight the BJP in Bengal.

recent_articles.title: Mamata Banerjee Sent Sourav Ganguly To Ask Yusuf Pathan To Quit As MP? What They Said
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sourav Ganguly** and **Yusuf Pathan** have both denied allegations that they were asked to vacate their seats for **Mamata Banerjee**.  A Bengal daily reported that the Trinamool Congress was seeking Ganguly's help to convince Pathan to step down from his Baharampur seat, but Pathan refuted these claims. The reports surfaced amidst a political crisis within the party and as **Banerjee** prepares for a comeback in Bengal politics.

recent_articles.title: Rs 1 lakh crore rail overhaul for Bengal: Vaishnaw, CM Adhikari review status of ongoing projects | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw** and **Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari** announced plans to overhaul the state's railway network, with over Rs 1 lakh crore worth of projects set for implementation. The projects include redeveloping 102 stations as "Amrit Bharat stations" and constructing 538 flyovers and underpasses to ease traffic congestion. **Vaishnaw** praised Adhikari for the BJP's victory in the state, while **Adhikari** pledged cooperation between the state government and the Centre on railway projects.  The meeting aimed to address delays caused by land acquisition issues and project clearances.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Police recover large cache of arms hidden inside pond at Sandeshkhali - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **West Bengal Police's Special Task Force (STF)** recovered a large cache of firearms and ammunition hidden in a pond belonging to **Trinamool Congress** functionaries Robin Das and Gopal Das in Sandeshkhali, North 24 Parganas district.  **Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari** praised the police for this major breakthrough, stating that it was part of efforts to restore law and order after years of illegal weapon use under the previous Trinamool regime. **Rekha Patra**, a BJP MLA who survived the Sandeshkhali violence in 2024, welcomed the recovery as a step towards normalcy.

recent_articles.title: 'Undermined Under Abhishek Banerjee': Trinamool Minority Cell Leader Quits
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mohammed Ajmal Siddique**, former State Secretary (Minority Cell) of the **Trinamool Congress**, resigned from all party posts and primary membership on Saturday. He cited personal reasons, dissatisfaction with the party's atmosphere and functioning, and concerns about the democratic spirit and treatment of hardworking workers as factors in his decision.  Siddique also expressed displeasure with the leadership style of **Abhishek Banerjee**, the party's General Secretary.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Congress West Bengal MLA Ritabrata Banerjee To NDTV On What Next, "Backstabber" Label
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ritabrata Banerjee**, expelled Trinamool Congress MLA, is challenging the **Calcutta High Court** recognition of a rebel bloc as the main Opposition party in West Bengal.  **Kalyan Banerjee**, a senior Trinamool MP, has filed a petition contesting his claim to the post. **Ritabrata Banerjee** alleges forged signatures on party documents and claims that the rebel bloc's strength is higher than what was publicly acknowledged. The case hinges on whether the political party or the legislature party appoints the whip and leader, with parallels drawn from the Maharashtra political saga.

recent_articles.title: Trinamool Congress West Bengal MLA Ritabrata Banerjee To NDTV On What Next, "Backstabber" Label
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ritabrata Banerjee**, expelled Trinamool Congress MLA, is challenging the recognition of a rebel bloc as the main Opposition party in West Bengal's assembly. **Kalyan Banerjee**, a senior Trinamool MP and lawyer, filed a petition in the Calcutta High Court contesting the Speaker's decision. **Ritabrata Banerjee** alleges forged signatures on party documents and claims that the rebellion is a result of a "boss culture" and mistreatment by Abhishek Banerjee, who he credits with bringing him into the Trinamool. He also suggests that former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee should remain as "chief advisor" to the rebel bloc despite her criticism of his actions.

recent_articles.title: Glass ceiling: ‘Visibility is not equality, symbolism is not power’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Women politicians** from various parties, including **Sagarika Ghose**, **Aparajita Sarangi**, and **Dr. Thamizhachi Thangapandian**, participated in a panel discussion at the Hindu Huddle in Bengaluru on Saturday. They discussed the need for more inclusive spaces for women in public life, arguing that the concept of a "glass ceiling" is inaccurate and flawed. The panelists emphasized the importance of dismantling deep-rooted patriarchy and promoting greater political representation for women.  They also highlighted the significance of cultural shifts towards valuing women's contributions and advocating for increased opportunities for women in politics.

recent_articles.title: Relief material recoveries put several Trinamool leaders under scanner; many arrested, others face protest - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Trinamool Congress** leaders across West Bengal have faced scrutiny and protests following allegations of hoarding and diverting government relief materials meant for disaster-stricken residents.  Recovered supplies included blankets, tarpaulins, clothes, rice, and wheat from the residences and quarters of several prominent figures, including **Udeep Singh**, **Giasuddin Molla**, and **Narendranath Chakraborty**. Protests erupted outside these locations as locals expressed frustration over the lack of relief aid.  The incidents have sparked criticism in political circles, with some accusing the party of prioritizing personal gain over the needs of vulnerable communities.

recent_articles.title: Suresh Wadkar met wife Padma when she was 8: ‘Why shouldn’t I marry her?’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suresh Wadkar**, a veteran playback singer, shared his love story with wife **Padma Wadkar**.  He revealed that their bond grew stronger after he underwent bypass surgery and that spiritual leader **Sathya Sai Baba** predicted their marriage. The couple married in 1998 when **Padma** was 24 years old.  Wadkar also addressed rumors about his past connection to actor **Madhuri Dixit**, stating he is grateful for finding a "Madhuri named Padma" in his life.

recent_articles.title: NIA Arrests Ex-Trinamool MLA Saokat Molla In Bhangar Blast Case
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The National Investigation Agency (NIA)** arrested former Trinamool Congress MLA Saokat Molla, a prime suspect in the Bhangar bomb blast case, from West Bengal's South 24 Parganas district.  Molla was declared 'absconding' earlier this week after the agency conducted searches at his residence and other locations linked to him. The arrest brings the total number of individuals held in connection with the case to four. Molla will be produced before a court tomorrow, and further legal proceedings will follow.

recent_articles.title: TMC parliamentary split ‘just a matter of time’: As Mamata fights back, cracks grow | Political Pulse News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee** is facing growing dissent within the **Trinamool Congress (TMC)**, with 60 of its 80 MLAs in West Bengal signaling rebellion.  Senior TMC leader Sukhendu Sekhar Roy believes a similar reaction could occur in the Lok Sabha, where the party has 28 MPs and faces potential defections under anti-defection laws. The rebel faction is seeking to retain **Mamata Banerjee** as chairperson of the party, while others within the party are calling for her removal from leadership positions.  The situation remains fluid with some rebels expressing a desire to remain under **Mamata Banerjee's** leadership but disagreeing with Abhishek Banerjee's role as national general secretary.

recent_articles.title: In Who-Is-Real-Trinamool Fight, Pushback Planned Against Ritabrata Banerjee
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**'s faction of the **Trinamool Congress** is challenging the Speaker's recognition of **Ritabrata Banerjee** as the new Leader of the Opposition. The faction is also attempting to reintegrate rebel MLAs into the original party fold.  Senior MLA Soven Deb Chatterjee has stated that many rebels are returning to the original Trinamool fold, rejecting **Ritabrata Banerjee**'s list of rebels. Meanwhile, a group of loyalists met at **Mamata Banerjee**'s house and reaffirmed their support for her leadership.

recent_articles.title: Only 8 MLAs, 6 MPs At Mamata Banerjee's Home For Key Meet. Party Clarifies
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Only eight **Trinamool Congress** MLAs attended a National Working Committee meeting at former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee's Kalighat house in Kolkata, following a rebellion within the party.  The party clarified that not all MPs and MLAs were invited, with only four Lok Sabha MPs and two Rajya Sabha MPs present. **Abhishek Banerjee**, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, was among those who attended. Rebel MLA **Ritabrata Banerjee** stated that more MLAs will join the rebellion, increasing the number of supporters beyond 2/3rd of the party.

recent_articles.title: Bandar movie review: Bobby Deol anchors Anurag Kashyap’s strongest film in years | Movie-review News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anurag Kashyap**'s film "Bandar" explores the complexities of a man accused of rape and the woman who claims to be his victim.  The film delves into themes of gender dynamics, privilege, and the Me-Too movement, prompting viewers to question their own moral boundaries. **Bobby Deol**, in a career-defining performance, portrays a washed-out entertainer facing accusations of sexual assault. The supporting cast includes **Sanya Malhotra**, **Riddhi Sen**, and **Sapna Pabbi**.  The film's unique style and thought-provoking narrative make it a compelling watch.

recent_articles.title: Daily Briefing: Monsoon arrives in Kerala; 45 major paper leaks in 24 years, who’s accountable? | Live News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) declared the onset of the southwest monsoon on Thursday, three days later than usual. The monsoon is expected to bring below-normal rainfall this year due to the El Niño weather pattern. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** discussed deepening cooperation in energy and other areas with **Acting President Delcy Rodríguez** of Venezuela during talks in India.  The IMD has forecast below-normal rainfall this year at 90% of the long-period average, largely due to the developing El Niño weather pattern, which typically weakens monsoon rains and pushes temperatures higher. The monsoon is now expected to advance towards Goa, Maharashtra and more parts of southern India over the next few days.

recent_articles.title: Bidhannagar Corporation Mayor resigns a day after Kolkata Corporation Mayor quit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Krishna Chakraborty**, the **Bidhannagar Municipality Corporation** Mayor, resigned on Thursday (June 4, 2026), citing personal reasons. **Chakraborty** has served as a councillor for 16 years and stated she will continue to work in that capacity.  Her resignation comes after **Firhad Hakim**, the former **Kolkata Municipal Corporation** mayor, submitted his resignation on Wednesday (June 3, 2026). The West Bengal government criticized both resignations, calling them irresponsible and lacking accountability. The KMC elections are scheduled for December 2026.

recent_articles.title: Bengal Ex-Minister's Brother Arrested Over Extortion Charges In Kolkata

The BJP won a landslide victory in the state elections, ending 15 years of rule by **Banerjee's All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)**. Adhikari's rise to power is marked by his controversial political career and his shift from a close ally of **Banerjee** to a leading figure within the BJP.  He will now face challenges including post-election violence, economic concerns, and deep political divisions in the state.

recent_articles.title: Punjab worse than West Bengal under AAP rule, says Haryana CM Saini - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini** criticized the **AAP government in Punjab**, accusing it of failing to control drug trafficking, illegal mining, and lawlessness. He compared the current situation in Punjab to West Bengal under **Mamata Banerjee**, stating that people are disillusioned with the AAP and seeking change through the BJP's governance model.  Saini also contrasted the BJP's policies with those of the Congress, highlighting the latter's corruption and lack of focus on people's welfare.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari** was unanimously elected leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party's legislature party in West Bengal following their victory in the recent assembly elections. **Amit Shah**, Union Home Minister, presided over the meeting and supported **Adhikari's** nomination.  The BJP secured 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress won 80.  **Adhikari** then met with Governor R.N. Ravi to formally stake his claim to form a government.

recent_articles.title: ​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** secured a resounding victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, winning 207 out of 294 seats.  **Suvendu Adhikari**, former Leader of the Opposition and now the new Chief Minister, defeated incumbent **Mamata Banerjee** in her own constituency, marking a significant shift in power dynamics. The BJP's success can be attributed to its strategic focus on booth-level organization, leveraging Hindu identity politics, and exploiting popular dissatisfaction with the TMC's governance.  The party's victory comes with challenges, including restoring law and order after targeted violence.

recent_articles.title: BJP’s victory in Bengal will plug a big hole in national security, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Amit Shah**, **Union Home Minister**, stated that the BJP's victory in West Bengal was significant for national security, as it plugs a major hole and will make infiltration and cattle smuggling impossible. He emphasized that this victory signifies ideological continuity for the party, marking its presence across all states from Gangotri to Gangasagar.  **Shah** also highlighted the importance of the victory in light of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 150th birth anniversary and thanked voters for their support. The BJP Legislature Party leader, **Suvendu Adhikari**, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister on May 9th.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal government formation LIVE: Amit Shah arrives in Kolkata for BJP legislature party meet to elect new CM - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The BJP legislature party** will meet in Kolkata on Friday, May 8, 2026, to elect its leader with **Suvendu Adhikari** emerging as the frontrunner.  Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the **TMC’s** 15-year rule, **Mamata Banerjee**, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with **Suvendu Adhikari’s** personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

recent_articles.title: Faced harassment from a group of men onboard Delhi-bound flight, alleges MP Mahua Moitra - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mahua Moitra**, a Trinamool Congress MP, alleged she was harassed by a group of men on an **IndiGo** flight to Delhi.  She shared video evidence of the incident and tagged **Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu** and **IndiGo** requesting action against those involved.  Moitra stated that she ignored the incident but later saw the video going viral and decided to publicly denounce it, adding she would file a formal complaint with the airline.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal Governor dissolves State Legislative Assembly - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. N. Ravi**, the Governor of West Bengal, dissolved the state's Legislative Assembly on May 7, 2026, ending the 17th assembly term. The move follows the BJP's victory in the recent assembly elections, securing a majority and leading to the end of **Mamata Banerjee**'s Trinamool Congress rule.  The swearing-in ceremony for the new BJP government is scheduled for Saturday, May 9, 2026, at the Brigade Parade Grounds.

recent_articles.title: Tensions high in West Bengal after BJP aide shot dead and hundreds arrested | India | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, **Tensions** have escalated with violence erupting and hundreds arrested.  **Chandranath Rath**, an aide to the BJP leader **Suvendu Adhikari**, was shot dead, prompting accusations of political killings by the **TMC**, who allege widespread irregularities. The state police chief has registered over 200 criminal cases and arrested 433 individuals for their involvement in post-election violence.  The **BJP** denies all allegations of wrongdoing while the **TMC** vows to challenge the election results in the Supreme Court.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh seeks China support for Teesta restoration project - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh**’s new government has sought **China's** involvement in the Teesta River restoration project, a move that could strain relations with **India**.  The **Bangladesh** government is seeking to increase its share of the river's water under the 2011 Teesta water-sharing treaty, which has been blocked by **West Bengal**’s outgoing Chief Minister, **Mamata Banerjee**.  **China's** Foreign Minister, **Wang Yi**, pledged support for **Bangladesh's** new government and its development goals.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election: Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandranath Rath shot dead in post-poll violence
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, personal assistant to **Suvendu Adhikari**, a top BJP leader, was shot and killed in West Bengal after the state election.  Police are investigating but haven't made any arrests. The incident is part of escalating tensions following the BJP's historic victory, which ended 15 years of rule by **Mamata Banerjee**'s Trinamool Congress (TMC).  The TMC condemned the killing and demanded accountability for those responsible. Both parties have accused each other of violence and intimidation, with the BJP alleging a deterioration in law and order under **Banerjee**. The new chief minister is expected to be sworn in on Saturday.

recent_articles.title: Tension grips parts of North 24 Parganas after murder of Suvendu’s aide; security tightened - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tension** prevailed in parts of West Bengal's North 24 Parganas district following the shooting death of **Chandranath Rath**, a close aide of BJP leader **Suvendu Adhikari**.  Police deployed additional forces in Madhyamgram, Doharia and surrounding areas after **BJP** supporters protested for the immediate arrest of the assailants. The incident has been described as a "targeted assassination" by the **BJP**, while the **TMC** denies any involvement. Police are conducting raids and examining CCTV footage to identify the perpetrators.

recent_articles.title: Motorbike gunmen kill BJP political aide in India's West Bengal - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, a political aide to **Suvendu Adhikari**, the leader of the opposition in West Bengal's assembly, was shot and killed on Wednesday near his home in Kolkata.  Rath was ambushed by gunmen on motorbikes who opened fire on his vehicle, resulting in multiple gunshot wounds. The killing is the latest in a series of violent incidents since the results of the state elections were announced last week. **Pritam Sengupta**, a doctor at Apollo Hospital, confirmed Rath's death.  The BJP has accused the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)** of responsibility for the murder, while the TMC denies any involvement and accuses the BJP of targeting their supporters.

recent_articles.title: Killing as revenge for Mamata’s loss in Bhabanipur: Mother of slain aide of Suvendu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath’s** mother demanded life imprisonment for the assailants who killed her son after he was shot by bike-borne attackers near Doltala in Madhyamgram. She claimed the killing was a result of **Mamata Banerjee**'s defeat against **Suvendu Adhikari** in Bhabanipur and that TMC leaders had made statements suggesting retribution for BJP workers following the election results.

recent_articles.title: CEC directs West Bengal officials to ensure zero post-poll violence - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar** directed West Bengal authorities to ensure zero tolerance for post-poll violence following three deaths linked to alleged incidents since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026. **Kumar** instructed authorities to immediately arrest those responsible for inciting violence and vandalism, with increased vigilance across districts by police and central forces. The West Bengal Assembly polls were held in two phases on April 23 and 29, with the BJP securing victory.

recent_articles.title: Slain Chandranath Rath: From air force serviceman to Suvendu’s trusted troubleshooter - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, a close aide of **Suvendu Adhikari**, the leader of the opposition in West Bengal, was shot dead on Wednesday night.  Rath had served in the Indian Air Force for nearly two decades before transitioning into political coordination and administrative roles. He joined **Adhikari's** inner circle around 2019 after a brief stint in the corporate sector. Rath played a key role in several high-profile political battles, including the BJP’s Bhabanipur campaign, and was considered a trusted confidant of **Adhikari**.  His death has sparked strong reactions in Bengal and heightened tensions following the Assembly election results.

recent_articles.title: 65% of newly elected Bengal MLAs face criminal cases; 61% are ‘crorepatis’: ADR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR)** reported that 65% of newly elected legislators in the **West Bengal Assembly** have declared criminal cases, a significant increase from previous elections.  Of these, 58% face serious charges, including murder and attempt to murder. The report also found that 74% of winning candidates from the **Bharatiya Janata Party** and 43% from the **All India Trinamool Congress** have declared criminal cases.  The total assets of all winning candidates stand at ₹1,091 crore, with an average asset of Rs 3.73 crore per MLA. The report also highlighted concerns about the rising wealth among elected representatives and under-representation of women in the legislature.

recent_articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant shot dead - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chandranath Rath**, personal assistant to **Suvendu Adhikari**, the BJP leader, was shot and killed in Madhyamgram, West Bengal on Wednesday (May 6, 2026).  The incident occurred during post-poll violence in the state. **Samik Bhattacharya**, the **West Bengal BJP** president, and **Adhikari** urged party supporters to avoid violence. The **Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar** directed authorities to ensure zero tolerance towards post-poll violence and arrest those involved.  The **Trinamool Congress** condemned the deaths of Rath and other TMC workers killed in violence across the state.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal CM refuses to resign after poll defeat - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, the chief minister of West Bengal, refused to resign after her party lost power in state elections to the **BJP**.  The BJP secured over two-thirds of the seats, marking a significant political milestone for the party. **Banerjee** claimed that 100 seats were "forcibly taken" from her party and accused the **Election Commission** of bias. The **Chief Electoral Officer**, **Manoj Kumar Agarwal**, dismissed these allegations as baseless.  The state's governor can demand Banerjee's resignation or wait until her term ends, at which point a new government will be formed.

recent_articles.title: ‘Defeated by conspiracy’: West Bengal chief minister refuses to resign after election loss | India | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Mamata Banerjee**, India's most powerful female politician, has refused to resign as chief minister of West Bengal despite the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** winning a landslide victory in state elections.  Banerjee claims the election was "looted" by conspiracy and that she will not step down. The governor of West Bengal has threatened to send police if Banerjee does not voluntarily relinquish her position, potentially leading to legal challenges. The BJP has responded with accusations of "constitutional blasphemy" and a ban on advisors appointed by Banerjee from entering their offices.  Banerjee's refusal to step down could lead to further political turmoil in the state.

recent_articles.title: Four killed in post-election violence in India’s West Bengal | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the **Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s** Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) sweeping victory in West Bengal's state election, at least four people have been killed in political unrest. The BJP claimed two of its workers were killed while the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)** party reported two of their workers being beaten to death.  The violence erupted after the results were announced and included clashes between rival supporters in Kolkata and other districts, with allegations of vandalism and attacks on party offices from both sides. The Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed state officials to enforce “zero tolerance” towards post-poll violence.

recent_articles.title: Women voters rejected Congress, allies for opposing Reservation Bill, says Nandyal MP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Byreddy Shabari**, **TDP national general secretary**, stated that women voters have rejected the Congress, DMK, and Trinamool Congress for opposing the Women’s Reservation Bill.  Shabari claimed these parties were responsible for the bill's defeat in Parliament and that women voters delivered a "fitting lesson" by defeating them in recent elections. She expressed confidence that the NDA government will pass the bill soon and implement the 33% reservation for women.

recent_articles.title: What happens if a Chief Minister refuses to relinquish office after electoral defeat? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, **Mamata Banerjee**, chairperson of the **Trinamool Congress**, refused to resign as Chief Minister, claiming the results were a result of a conspiracy.  She stated that the election was not conducted fairly and accused the BJP of misusing central forces. However, legal experts suggest that an election petition can be filed challenging the results based on allegations of voter deletion during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in West Bengal. The tenure of the current Assembly ends on May 7, at which point a new government will be formed.
